doc.night_duty.title: St. Agnes Home for Children
doc.night_duty.body: Lights out at nine. Any child found out of bed is to stand in the corridor until I say otherwise. The Hale boy again. He says the little girl in white told him to come down. There is no little girl in white.
clue.locked_linen: The linen cupboard is locked. Sister would keep that key close.
clue.locked_west_dorm: The west dorm won’t open. There’s no keyhole. It’s bolted from the inside.
clue.took_office_key: A key in the washroom drain, tagged “Office”. Someone dropped it in a hurry.
clue.took_linen_key: Sister's desk held a key tagged “Linen”.
clue.read_night_duty: Sister M. punished children found out of bed. The Hale boy talked about a little girl in white.

whisper.rewind.dark: Don't stay in the dark so long. They get in.
whisper.tommy.follow: Come on. Before she checks the beds.
whisper.tommy.washroom: She scrubbed her hands every night. Every single night.
whisper.tommy.names: Follow me. They put the names wrong.
whisper.tommy.cubbies: Everyone had their own shelf. Everyone.
msg.platesSolved: Every name is where it belongs. Something small rolls out from under bed 2.
item.plate.name: Name plate: {name}
item.plate.desc: Tin plate from a bed. Someone scratched at the screws.
item.toy_ball.name: Rubber ball
item.toy_doll.name: Rag doll
item.toy_doll.desc: One button eye. The other is sewn shut.
item.toy_top.name: Spinning top
item.toy_top.desc: Blue and yellow. Still spins true.
item.statue_piece.name: Statue piece
item.statue_piece.desc: A stone hand, broken off a statue at the wrist. The rest of her must be somewhere in this building.
doc.dorm_register.title: Dormitory register
doc.dorm_register.body:
Boys' dormitory, east. Beds as allotted.
1. Walter Price
2. Thomas Hale (“Tommy”)
3. Peter Doyle
4. Sam Pike
5. Alfred Burns (“Alfie”)
6. Arthur Lowe
7. George Finch
8. Frank Ellery
9. Harry Moss
10. Ernest Dunn
No child to change beds without leave.
clue.read_dorm_register: The dorm register lists who slept in each numbered bed. Bed 2 was Thomas Hale. Tommy. Hale, the same name as on my file.
msg.toysSolved: Every toy is home. Down the corridor, a bolt slides back on its own.
clue.took_toy_ball: A red ball in the linen cupboard. Somebody hid it there.
clue.took_toy_doll: A rag doll by the washroom drain. One eye sewn shut.
clue.took_toy_top: A spinning top on the dining hall floor, by the wall.
clue.solved_toys: I put the toys back in their cubbies. The west dorm is open now.
clue.solved_plates: The name plates are back on the right beds. Tommy’s bed gave up a little brass crank.
msg.cubbyEmpty: Empty. Something of theirs should be here.
msg.platesNeedClue: I don’t know whose beds these were. There must be a record somewhere.
msg.toyNeedsClue: Whose was this ({item})? One of the children must have drawn it.
msg.musicBoxNoCrank: The winding key is missing. It won’t play without it.
msg.musicBoxWound: The crank fits. The box ticks, waiting.
msg.lullabySolved: The tune carries on by itself. Behind the east wall, something gives.
clue.saw_drawing_ivy: Ivy drew herself holding a red ball.
clue.saw_drawing_rose: Rose drew herself with her rag doll.
clue.saw_drawing_peter: Peter drew himself with a spinning top.
doc.lullaby_chalk.title: A slate on the playroom wall
doc.lullaby_chalk.body:
A row of little pictures over a wavy line, with a crooked music note at the end:
star, star, moon, bird, moon, heart.
The chalk is fresh.
clue.read_lullaby_chalk: Someone chalked a tune as pictures: star, star, moon, bird, moon, heart.
doc.hale_file_1.title: St. Agnes Home for Children
doc.hale_file_1.body:
Name: T. Hale. Age: [[blot]]
Brought by: the parish. Parents: none living.
Notes: Quiet. Talks to children who are not there. Sister M. recommends the quiet room until he stops.
clue.read_hale_file_1: Page one of a file on T. Hale. The same name as on my file. They kept him in the quiet room.
clue.took_toy_horse: Tommy’s wooden horse. It was in the quiet room, where they kept him.
clue.took_statue_piece: A stone hand from a statue of a saint. The rest of her must be somewhere in St. Agnes. I should keep it.
clue.solved_lullaby: I played the chalked tune on the music box. A hidden door opened in the west dorm.
msg.mapTaken: A plan of the wing. Added to the journal (J, MAPS).
msg.mapPencilled: I pencil the room onto the map.
clue.visited_quiet_room: The quiet room. Small, bare, a drawing of a horse on the wall. It’s on my map now.
intro.whisper2: Find our things. Then we can all go to sleep.
item.flashlight.name: Flashlight
look.drawing.house: A house with a red roof and one door. Someone drew it over and over.
look.drawing.horse: A wooden horse, drawn very carefully. A name underneath has been rubbed out.
look.drawing.children: Children holding hands in a row. One at the end is only an outline.
look.drawing.sun: A yellow sun over green grass. Outside.
look.drawing.skipping: A girl in a red dress, skipping. It wasn’t here before.
msg.lockedAway: The cabinet is locked. There’s a little bulb in the lock, dark.
msg.fusesPowerOn: The lights are on. Better not touch it.
msg.fusesNeedClue: Four levers, numbered. Someone must have written down which order.
msg.fusesWrong: The levers snap back up with a crack.
msg.fusesSolved: Light floods back down the corridor. Across the room, the cabinet lock clicks open.
msg.lightsOut: Every light in the wing dies at once.
doc.night_rota.title: Night duty rota
doc.night_rota.body: If the lights fail, do not wake the children. Go to the fuse box in the sick bay and pull the levers in the order of tonight’s hymns (see the board in the dining hall). Any other order and the box trips again.
clue.read_night_rota: If the lights fail: the fuse box in the sick bay, levers in the order of tonight’s hymns, on the board in the dining hall.
clue.saw_hymn_board: Tonight’s hymns, on the dining hall board: 3, 1, 4, 2.
clue.solved_fuses: I got the lights back on. The medicine cabinet in the sick bay opened by itself.
doc.punishment_book.title: Punishment book
doc.punishment_book.body:
Monday. Two out of bed after lights out. Corridor until midnight.
Tuesday. The Hale boy, talking in the dark again. The quiet room.
Wednesday. The Hale boy.
Thursday. The Hale boy. He says he is not afraid of the quiet room. He will be.
clue.read_punishment_book: Sister M.’s punishment book. Tommy is in it almost every night. Always the quiet room.
doc.letter_peter.title: A page from a diary
doc.letter_peter.body:
Tuesday.
I lent Tommy my spinning top and he gave it back the very next day, like he promised.
Then Sister took it and hid it in the dining hall, so I would cry at supper.
I did not cry. I will not cry tomorrow either.
clue.read_letter_peter: Peter’s diary: Sister hid his spinning top in the dining hall to make him cry.
doc.letter_rose.title: A note under a pillow
doc.letter_rose.body: The music box only plays for Tommy. He says the lady in the walls likes it. I don’t like the lady in the walls.
clue.read_letter_rose: Rose wrote that the music box only plays for Tommy, and that a “lady in the walls” likes it.
doc.nurse_log.title: Sick bay log
doc.nurse_log.body:
Three in with the cough. Gave linctus.
T. Hale brought in again from the quiet room, cold to the touch, no fever. Would not say who he had been talking to.
The cabinet lock is on the lighting circuit. When the fuses go, so does the key.
clue.read_nurse_log: The nurse’s log: the medicine cabinet’s lock runs on the lights. When the fuses go, it stays shut.
doc.menu_card.title: This week’s menu
doc.menu_card.body:
Monday: porridge, bread and dripping.
Tuesday: porridge, boiled potatoes.
Wednesday: porridge.
Thursday: porridge.
Children who leave food will have it again at breakfast.
clue.took_battery: A spare battery for the flashlight, for when the light runs low.
msg.batteryIn: Fresh battery in. The beam steadies.
tutorial.inventory: {open} shows what you carry. Pick an item, then {use} to use it.
whisper.tommy.wall: She puts him behind the wall when he cries. Rose knows.
tutorial.move: {keys} to walk, the mouse to look around.
tutorial.pause: ESC pauses the tape. Controls and settings are under SETUP.
tutorial.run: Hold {key} to run. It is loud, and it tires you.

tutorial.lean: {left} and {right} lean to peek round corners.

doc.rose_bed_note.title: A note on Rose’s bed
doc.rose_bed_note.body: Tommy only plays the music box with the song from the playroom slate. Then the wall lets him in. I watched.
clue.read_rose_bed_note: Rose wrote that Tommy plays the music box with the song from the playroom slate, and then the wall lets him in.
card.title: NEW ITEM
card.flashlight.body: The dark wears on your mind; light keeps it steady. It runs on batteries.
card.battery.body: For the flashlight. Each one lasts about eight minutes of light.
card.battery.use: {battery}  swap it in when the light runs low
card.pills.body: No label. They steady the hands and the mind when everything starts to slip.
item.pills.short: Unlabelled pills. They steady the mind.
item.toy_ball.short: A red rubber ball. Whose was it?
item.toy_doll.short: A rag doll with one button eye.
item.toy_top.short: A blue and yellow spinning top.
item.statue_piece.short: A stone hand from a statue.
item.plate.short: A tin name plate from a bed.
card.sanity.title: YOUR MIND
card.sanity.body:
The dark, the children and what you see here wear on your mind. Light, your room and pills steady it.

Your pulse (lower left) shows how much is left. If your mind gives way, you black out and the tape rewinds to your last checkpoint.
card.sanity.after:
Your mind gave way, so the tape rewound to your last checkpoint.

Keep the flashlight on, stay near lights, rest in your room or take pills before the pulse runs out.

clue.saw_class_painting: A class painting of five children in a row, left to right: Agnes, Tommy, Maggie, Sam, Edith. Underneath: Those who have left us.
item.headmaster_key.name: Headmaster's key
item.headmaster_key.short: A brass key with a paper tag: HEAD.
item.headmaster_key.desc: It dropped out of the piano when the song came out right.
item.matches.name: Matches
item.matches.short: A box of matches, nearly full.
item.matches.desc: For the grave lanterns. One match each.
item.skipping_rope.name: Skipping rope
item.skipping_rope.desc: Worn smooth at the handles. She gave it to you herself.
item.stone_lamb.name: Stone lamb
item.stone_lamb.short: A small stone lamb from a statue.
item.stone_lamb.desc: St. Agnes is often shown with a lamb in her arms. This one would fit the crook of a stone arm.
doc.library_ticket.title: Library ticket
doc.library_ticket.body:
Borrower: Margaret Rowe, Form II
Book: Songs for Little Voices
Due back: 25th March
NOT RETURNED. Borrower struck off.
On the back, in pencil: if you find my book you can keep the song
clue.read_library_ticket: Maggie's library ticket: Songs for Little Voices, never brought back. The card index should say which shelf.
doc.my_song.title: My song
doc.my_song.body:
Six coloured shapes in a row: a blue star, a blue star, a yellow triangle, a purple cross, a blue star, a yellow triangle.
Underneath: play it on the piano, not out loud.
clue.read_my_song: Maggie's song is six coloured shapes: blue star, blue star, yellow triangle, purple cross, blue star, yellow triangle. It's for the piano.
doc.maggie_note.title: A folded note
doc.maggie_note.byline: Maggie, in a coat pocket, with the matches
doc.maggie_note.body:
I'm not allowed to tell, so I sing it instead.
If you can hear me singing, you're the same as us.
Don't let her catch you looking away.
M.
clue.read_maggie_note: A note from Maggie, left with the matches: if I can hear her singing, I'm the same as them.
doc.detention_book.title: Detention book
doc.detention_book.body:
Monday. Rowe, M.: telling tales about the orphanage. Lines: I must not tell (100).
Tuesday. Rowe, M.: the same. Lines (200). Headmaster informed.
Wednesday. Hale, T.: talking during prayers. Sent to the boiler house for coal. Not back for the afternoon register.
Thursday. Hale, T.: absent.
Friday. Rowe, M.: absent. The Headmaster says she has been moved to the west wing. Desk to be cleared.
clue.read_detention_book: Miss Pruett's detention book. Maggie was punished for telling. Tommy was sent to the boiler house for coal and wasn't back for the afternoon register.
doc.fire_drill_log.title: Fire drill log
doc.fire_drill_log.body:
3rd March. Bell at 10.02. All out in 2 min 40. All accounted for.
7th April. Bell at 2.15. All out in 2 min 10. All accounted for.
The fire, night of 12th May. Dormitories cleared by Sister M. All accounted for except Hale, T.
19th May. Drill cancelled by the Headmaster. No reason given.
clue.read_fire_drill_log: The fire-drill log: after the fire, everyone was accounted for except T. Hale.
doc.unsent_letter.title: An unsent letter
doc.unsent_letter.body:
Headmaster,
Margaret Rowe came to me again on Tuesday about the quiet room in the orphanage. She says a boy is kept in it for days, and that she heard him scratching at the door.
I told her not to tell tales and set her lines, as you asked.
I am no longer sure I was right. Where is she now? Her desk has not been touched.
L. P.
clue.read_unsent_letter: Miss Pruett never sent her letter. Maggie told her a boy was locked in the quiet room for days. Then Maggie was gone.
rhyme.class1.1: One for the ink and two for the chalk,
rhyme.class1.2: three for the girl who was not let talk,
rhyme.class1.3: four for my name that is under the lid,
rhyme.class1.4: five for the lady who saw what you did.
rhyme.library.2: turn around quickly: what do you see?
rhyme.library.3: Stone in the doorway, stone on the stair,
rhyme.library.4: shut your eyes once and she's already there.
rhyme.gym.1: Two for the chalk and seven for the bell,
rhyme.gym.2: five for the lady who watches as well,
rhyme.gym.3: nine for the girl who would not keep still,
rhyme.gym.4: and one for the boy who sleeps up the hill.
rhyme.staff.1: Who took the matches? Who stole the light?
rhyme.staff.2: Somebody's coat has them tucked out of sight.
rhyme.staff.3: Grey coats, grey coats, hanging in a row,
rhyme.staff.4: look for the one with a ribbon bow.
maggie.library.still: She only moves when nobody's looking.
maggie.library.leaving: The dark counts as not looking. Keep a light on her.
maggie.music: I put the colours on the piano, so the little ones could play.
maggie.corridor: I told Miss about the quiet room. After that I wasn't allowed to talk.
maggie.courtyard: Tommy used to wait for me by the gate. Then he stopped coming.
watcher.catch.1: You looked away. She only moves when nobody's looking.
watcher.catch.2: Didn't you hear her breathe? She only breathes when she's close.
watcher.catch.3: The dark is hers. Keep her in the light.
watcher.catch.4: Shut a door on her. She can't open doors.
watcher.catch.5: You blinked. Don't let your eyes close near her.
maggie.blackout: Too long in the dark. It gets inside you.

doc.struck_off.title: Struck off the roll
doc.struck_off.body:
Pupils struck off, in order:
1. Agnes. No surname. By the Founder's order. [[blot]]
2. Hale, Thomas. Aged 9. 2nd February.
3. Rowe, Margaret. Aged 8. 18th March. To the west wing.
4. Pike, Samuel. Aged 10. 9th June.
5. Carr, Edith. Aged 7. 30th October. To the west wing.
No further enquiries to be answered.
clue.read_struck_off: The roll, in the order they were struck off: Agnes, Thomas Hale, Margaret Rowe, Samuel Pike, Edith Carr. Five names, five graves.
doc.hale_file_2.title: St. Agnes Home for Children
doc.hale_file_2.body:
Schooling: Form II, Miss Pruett. Reads well. Will not do sums.
Conduct: talks in the dark; says a girl called Aggie stays with him.
Struck off the roll: 2nd February.
Re-admitted: 2nd February, the same night. No one remembers bringing him back.
Age on re-admission: [[blot]]
clue.read_hale_file_2: Page two of T. Hale’s file. Struck off the roll on 2nd February, and re-admitted the same night. Nobody remembers bringing him back.
doc.medical_card.title: Medical card
doc.medical_card.body:
Height 4 ft 1 in. Weight 3 st 2 lb. Two teeth missing.
Eyes good. Chest clear. Sleeps badly; walks at night.
Says a girl called Aggie keeps him company.
Referred to the doctor in the west wing, for his nerves. By order of Sister M.
clue.read_medical_card: Tommy's medical card. He walked in his sleep, talked about a girl called Aggie, and was sent to the doctor in the west wing.
doc.inspector_report.title: Inspector's report
doc.inspector_report.byline: Visit to St. Agnes School. R. Dale, Schools Inspector
doc.inspector_report.body:
Classrooms clean, children neat and very quiet. Too quiet, perhaps; none of them would look at me.
The registers show many gaps. The Headmaster explains these as transfers to the west wing for medical care.
I asked to see the west wing and was told the doctor does not receive visitors.
Recommendation: [[blot]]
clue.read_inspector_report: A schools inspector noticed the gaps in the registers. Nobody would let him see the west wing.
doc.venn_letter.title: A letter
doc.venn_letter.byline: Dr. A. Venn, the west wing, to the Headmaster
doc.venn_letter.body:
Dear Ashby,
The two you sent me in March have been most useful. My work goes well.
I shall need more. Children of eight to ten do best.
Send them at night, by the back stairs, so as not to upset the others. Their names need not trouble the register.
A. V.
clue.read_venn_letter: A letter to the headmaster from Dr. Venn of the west wing, asking for more children, to be sent at night. I don't want to know what for.
